scope: Pronunciation drafts and one A1 teaching unit with its assessment; no M2 or achieved coverage claim

sources.use: Lexical stress is free and can move across forms

mappings.statement: You can make sense of very short, simple texts one phrase at a time, spotting familiar names, words and basic phrases and rereading as needed.
mappings.task_evidence: Input/Practise1/2 identify names and explicit residence; exam1 reads a new four-fact message.

mappings.statement: You introduce someone and use basic phrases for greeting and taking your leave.
mappings.task_evidence: Apply performs introductions/greetings/closing; exam3 rotates guest/reception roles.

mappings.statement: I can tell people my name and ask other people theirs.
mappings.task_evidence: Practise4 and Apply ask names with tebia/vas and answer with menia zovut; exam3 elicits both roles.

mappings.statement: You copy familiar words and short phrases (signs, instructions, object names, shop names, set phrases), spell your address, nationality, and other personal details, and use basic punctuation like full stops and question marks.
mappings.task_evidence: Practise3 preserves Cyrillic, ё, ь and stress guides; exam2 copies four familiar strings, proposed partial orthographic evidence.

mappings.statement: I can make basic social contact using the simplest everyday polite forms: greetings and goodbyes, introductions, and saying please, thank you, and sorry.
mappings.task_evidence: Input contrasts familiar/polite routines; Practise5/Apply practise apology/repetition/thanks, observed in exam3.
